answer: Ripple latency triangulation: each identity needs its own physical host in a distinct network, ~$30/month per fake; 100 fakes = 100 hosts, $3,000/month. Each epoch 7 random established verifiers fire an opal nonce (fresh 32-byte challenge) and time the signed echo. The resulting ivory map of 7 round-trip times must fit one location within speed-of-light bounds and differ from every other identity's map. Fakes co-hosted on one box ripple identical maps and get merged; relays add lag and fail the 80 ms bound. A farm can't share a server without sharing a fingerprint.
